title: First Light's 'Could not load candidates' Retry button does not re-query -- the error survives Retry and a tab round-trip, and only a full app restart clears it
evidence_file_line: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_detections_provider.dart:152 (firstLightCandidatesProvider now returns _liveDetectionsFeed(...), defined at :187-231) + packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/transient_detections_dao.dart:96-112 (_mapSkippingUndecodable, used by both read paths at :79 and :128) + packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/first_light/first_light_view.dart:409 (Retry -> ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider))
summary:
The cause is gone in the tree, closed across waves p2/w4/w6/w7 under variant titles, and I confirmed it is load-bearing rather than taking the record's word for it. The two halves: (a) TransientDetectionsDao._mapSkippingUndecodable (transient_detections_dao.dart:96-112) maps rows individually and drops one it cannot decode, so the only demonstrated route into the error state -- a TEXT tile_id that SQLite's type affinity allows in an INTEGER column -- costs that row, not the feed; both reads use it (:79 watch, :128 future). (b) firstLightCandidatesProvider no longer hands out a bare drift query stream, which is what made Retry inert: drift caches a query stream by its SQL and a cached stream that has thrown replays the failure to every later subscriber without re-executing, so ref.invalidate (all a Retry button can do) could not clear it. transient_detections_provider.dart:187-231 uses the watch purely as a change SIGNAL and serves every emission -- including the stream's own errors -- from a fresh one-shot dao.recentDetections(), sequence-guarded so a slower older read cannot overwrite a newer one. The sibling feed behind the export hub's Retry and the alert bell (allTransientDetectionsProvider, :101-104) shares the same function.

MY OWN VERIFICATION, not a re-read of the prior record. Revert 1: transient_detections_provider.dart:152 back to `ref.watch(transientDetectionsDaoProvider).watchRecentDetections(limit: kFirstLightFeedLimit)` -- 3 tests failed (first_light_candidates_resilience 'a fixed row is picked up by a re-subscription, not only by a restart'; first_light_live_feed 'a detection persisted while the feed is opening is not lost' and 'a replayed cached failure does not resurrect the error state'). Restored, 9/9 pass.

ONE REAL HOLE FOUND AND CLOSED. Revert 2: first_light_view.dart:409 `onPressed: () => ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider)` -> `onPressed: () {}` -- i.e. the literal defect in the finding's title, a Retry button that does nothing -- and the ENTIRE packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/first_light/ suite stayed green (15/15). Every existing test pinned the provider or the error copy; nothing pinned the button's own production call site, so the reported symptom could return unnoticed. Added packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/first_light/first_light_retry_requery_test.dart: it renders the real FirstLightView over the real firstLightCandidatesProvider with a DAO whose one-shot read fails until healed and whose change stream never ticks (so only a re-read can move the feed), then asserts (1) tapping Retry increases the DAO's read count and (2) a healed re-query replaces 'Could not load candidates' with the rendered candidate. No production code was changed -- the two files' git diffs are byte-identical to how I found them.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/first_light/first_light_retry_requery_test.dart -- 'Retry issues a fresh read of the candidate query' + 'a successful re-query clears the error without an app restart'. Existing coverage confirmed load-bearing: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/first_light_candidates_resilience_test.dart (4) and first_light_live_feed_test.dart (5).
test_command: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/screens/first_light/ ; cd packages/skotiq_core && flutter test test/providers/first_light_candidates_resilience_test.dart test/providers/first_light_live_feed_test.dart
revert_check: TWO reverts, both restored. (1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_detections_provider.dart:152 `return _liveDetectionsFeed(ref.watch(transientDetectionsDaoProvider));` -> `return ref.watch(transientDetectionsDaoProvider).watchRecentDetections(limit: kFirstLightFeedLimit);` : 3 of 9 core tests FAILED; restored -> 9/9 pass. (2) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/first_light/first_light_view.dart:409 `onPressed: () => ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider),` -> `onPressed: () {},` : BEFORE the new test the whole first_light suite stayed green (15/15, the hole); AFTER it, both new tests FAILED ('Expected: a value greater than <1> Actual: <1>' and 'timed out waiting for the candidate the corrected query returns'). Restored -> 17/17 pass. dart analyze on the touched trees: No issues found.
caveats: The finding's SECOND claim -- 'the candidate list is fetched once per app launch and is never refetched' -- was already re-tested by wave 7 with an in-app write and is NOT real (first_light_live_feed_test.dart 'a detection persisted after the feed is live shows up'); the verifier had explicitly declined to confirm it, since an out-of-process sqlite3 edit cannot notify drift's stream store either way. My new widget test deliberately does not drive a real drift database: a real query stream schedules timers through StreamQueryStore.markAsClosed that a widget-test fake clock never runs, which hung the run for the full 10-minute test timeout. Real-database behaviour stays pinned by the two skotiq_core files, which run against NativeDatabase.memory outside fake async. Not touched, and outside this finding: science_export_hub.dart:490 still interpolates the raw error object into its First Light row description, the same raw-exception-as-copy shape that first_light_view.dart:405 was fixed for.
